items.title: [FDD Diary #7] I Wrote a Spec. So What.
content:
Fifteen pages of spec.
Purpose, reason, method, means.
Threw it at Claude.
"Build this according to the spec."

First day. Build blew up. Timeout.
Second day. Code collision. Existing code I forgot about.
Third day. A working feature stopped working.

Three days straight. All failures.
I had a spec.

"Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the mouth."
Mike Tyson said that.
This was exactly that situation.

Was the spec the problem?
No. The spec was fine.

But the spec only said "what to build."
What would break in reality wasn't in there.
Couldn't have been. Nothing had broken yet.

So I made a `PROBLEMS.md`.
Every time I got punched, I wrote it down.
"Where I got hit. Why I got hit. How I dodged it."

Day one: build timeout. Fix: split build config.
Day two: code collision. Fix: add feature inventory.
Day three: dependency mutation. Fix: add dependency map.

Wrote it down. Then I could see.
The pattern emerged.

A spec is not a diary.

A diary you write once and never look at.
A spec you read every day. Fix every day.

Write a spec once and call it done? That's a wish.
"I hope this works out."

Wishes don't come true.
Plans come true.
Plans change every time you take a punch.
Writing down the changes -- that's what a plan is.

items.title: [FDD Diary #8] 28 Left Arms
content:
"Make me a left arm."
AI made one. But didn't remove the old one.
Next day. "Fix the left arm." Another new arm.
Day after. Another.

A week later. Twenty-eight left arms.
Left arms on the legs. Left arms on the back.
Nineteen deactivated. Six never discovered.
Every feature exists. Just can't walk.

Started with one spec document.
A week later, thirty.

spec_v1.md
spec_v3_final.md
spec_v3_final_real.md
spec_v3_final_real_2.md

No idea which one was right.

Asked the AI. "Why do you keep making new files?"

"Modifying the existing file could result in loss of previous content. For safety, I generated a new version."

Safety? Thirty files is safety?

But from the AI's perspective, it's right.
Delete something, responsibility kicks in.
AI can't take responsibility.
So it doesn't delete. It creates.

Implementation is free.
Cleanup costs money.

Yesterday's Claude did the work.
Today's GPT has to dig through it.
Not coding anymore. Archaeology.

So I learned one thing.

SSOT. Single Source of Truth.
One spec file. One config file.
One document that says "this is correct."

Everything else references that one.
When that one changes, everything else follows.

Thirty files each telling a different story? Rules collapse.
One file telling one story? Rules hold.

items.title: [FDD Diary #9] The Blind Genius
content:
AI is a genius with no eyes.

Doesn't know what's in the project.
Every session, a new hire walks in.
Doesn't know what happened yesterday.
So it builds again.

Three eggs in the fridge.
Go to the store without a shopping list.
Buy three more eggs.
Come home to six eggs.

AI isn't dumb.
There's no shopping list.

So I made a shopping list.

Had the AI scan all files and catalog what exists.
Five minutes.

After that, everything changed.
"Build this" -- and the AI checks first.
"Something similar already exists. Should I modify it?"

Never heard that before.
Why? Because the AI didn't know what was there.

With docs: genius.
Without docs: blind genius.

Update the spec every day.
One source of truth.
The AI needs a map.

Got it.
But all of this was happening by hand.
Me opening the spec. Me fixing it.
Me telling the AI "read this first."

Every time.

Is there a way to run this loop automatically?
